questions.text: Why can a learned semantic embedding retrieve "transaction was declined" for the query "my payment did not go through" even when exact words differ?

options.A: It replaces every query word with all dictionary synonyms before matching.
options.B: It assigns the same vector to all documents about customer support.
options.C: It ranks documents solely by their length and shared punctuation.
options.D: It can place expressions with similar meanings close together in vector space.

questions.explanation: Learned semantic representations can encode similarity beyond exact token overlap. The lesson’s TF-IDF toy does not itself learn synonym equivalence.

questions.text: You need to search a large corpus quickly, then improve relevance among the retrieved candidates. Which pipeline matches the lesson?

options.A: Retrieve candidates with a bi-encoder, then rerank query-document pairs with a cross-encoder.
options.B: Run a cross-encoder over every document, then store one query-independent score per document.
options.C: Average all corpus vectors into one vector, then return documents in insertion order.
options.D: Retrieve candidates by document length, then discard the query before reranking.

questions.explanation: Bi-encoders support precomputed document vectors for fast retrieval; cross-encoders jointly process query-document pairs for candidate reranking.

questions.text: SimpleEmbedder ignores words outside its fitted vocabulary and leaves zero vectors unnormalized. Its cosine function returns 0.0 if either norm is zero. What happens when every query word is outside the vocabulary?

options.A: The embedder expands its vocabulary and relearns all document vectors.
options.B: The query vector stays zero and every cosine similarity score is 0.0.
options.C: The query receives a unit vector and matches the shortest document.
options.D: Cosine scoring raises ZeroDivisionError before any results are returned.

questions.explanation: No known words contribute to the query vector. The zero-norm guard yields 0.0 against every indexed document, so ties do not establish semantic relevance.
